examples.english: I live in a two-story house.

examples.japanese: {二階建|にかいだ}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦バス→バス：00769_basu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}った→乗る：00511_noru⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{建物|たてもの}→建物：01458_tatemono⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{二階建|にかいだ}て⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。

notes:
{二階建|にかいだ}て describes a building with two floors. It functions as a noun and also modifies nouns with ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ ({二階建|にかいだ}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧).

FORMS:
⟦{二階|にかい}→二階：27513_nikai⟧ (second floor) + {建|だ}て (built structure). The {建|だ}て suffix indicates the number of stories.

STORY PATTERN ([number]{階建|かいだ}て):
- {一階建|いっかいだ}て: one-story
- {二階建|にかいだ}て: two-story (this word)
- {三階建|さんかいだ}て: three-story
- {五階建|ごかいだ}て: five-story

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {二階建|にかいだ}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧: two-story house
- {二階建|にかいだ}て⟦バス→バス：00769_basu⟧: double-decker bus
- {二階建|にかいだ}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一軒家|いっけんや}→一軒家：15138_ikkenya⟧: two-story detached house

USAGE:
Most residential houses in Japanese suburbs are {二階建|にかいだ}て. The typical layout has living areas on the ⟦{一階|いっかい}→一階：27512_ikkai⟧ (first floor) and bedrooms on the ⟦{二階|にかい}→二階：27513_nikai⟧ (second floor).
